text: A block $B_i$ of the group algebra $k[G]$ is said to have defect $0$ when its associated defect group $D_i$ is:
explanation: A block of defect $0$ has $D_i=\{e\}$ and contains a unique simple module. A full Sylow $p$-subgroup is the FULL-defect (most complex) case. The defect group is always a $p$-subgroup, so it is not all of $G$ in general; 'Borel subgroup' is a Lie-group notion irrelevant to finite-group blocks.
